# R2 — 1 Thess 2:1–16 Defense past (2318–2972)

**Coverage:** Full slice read (cache file lines 1–655 = raw lines 2318–2972). Weima BECNT: III Defense of Apostolic Actions and Absence (2:1–3:13) intro; A. Defense of Past Actions in Thessalonica (2:1–16) literary analysis (autobiography genre; apologetic vs paraenetic function; extent; structure); exegesis 2:1–12 (six main clauses: bold preaching, God-examined speech, infants, nursing mother, self-sufficient labor, father); exegesis 2:13–16 (word of God; Judean churches / Jews–Judeans / ephthasen wrath); Additional Notes on 2:7–16; Excursus 2 (textual reading of 2:7 nēpioi vs ēpioi). Closes with unit outline recapitulation.

**Source attribution:** All claims below are Weima’s positions/readings in this range unless noted as his report of other scholars. Locus = slice line numbers (L#) and 1 Thess verse locus.

**Out-of-range flag:** Full defense of authenticity of 2:13–16 (theological / historical / form-critical / linguistic arguments against interpolation) is **not** developed in this slice; Weima explicitly defers to “the commentary introduction” (L65). In-range treatment of interpolation is limited to (a) assumption of authenticity when delimiting 2:1–16 and (b) AD 70 / Pearson–Baur link under ephthasen options (L507).

---

## Claims

### Group A — Macrostructure: defense before exhortation; extent; structure

### C-R2-01 | Letter body: defense (2:1–3:13) before exhortation (4:1–5:22)
- **Claim (Weima):** Body falls into two major sections: first half (2:1–3:13) defends integrity of Paul’s motives/conduct; second half (4:1–5:22) exhorts. Defense logically precedes exhortations so Paul can reestablish trust before readers accept appeals.
- **Quote:** "The defense logically comes prior to the exhortations, since Paul first needs to reestablish his readers’ trust and confidence so that they will accept the appeals and encouragements he gives them later in the letter."
- **Locus:** L1–3 / 1 Thess 2:1–5:22 overview
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]], [[paul-apostle]]

### C-R2-02 | Defense half: past visit (2:1–16) then present absence (2:17–3:10); transitional prayers 3:11–13
- **Claim (Weima):** Extended defense is chronologically ordered: genuineness of past mission-founding visit (2:1–16), then present absence (2:17–3:10); closes with two transitional prayers (3:11 looks back; 3:12–13 looks ahead to exhortative half).
- **Quote:** "Paul first defends the genuineness of his past actions during his mission-founding visit to Thessalonica (2:1–16) and then defends his present absence from the believers in this city (2:17–3:10)."
- **Locus:** L3–5, L9–15 / 2:1–3:13 outline
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-03 | Opponents outside church: fellow citizens charge flattery/gain like wandering teachers
- **Claim (Weima):** Non-Christians—“fellow citizens” (2:14)—oppressed the church and questioned founder Paul as no different from wandering philosophers/teachers notorious for praise and financial gain. Thessalonian Christians had not bought the charges, but a young church under pressure needed answer.
- **Quote:** "They claimed that the apostle was no different from the wandering philosophers or traveling teachers of that day who had a notorious reputation for being interested solely in winning human praise and financial gain."
- **Locus:** L17–19, L59 / 2:1–16 intro
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-04 | 2:1–12 Paul/co-missionaries; 2:13–16 Thessalonians’ response as confirmatory
- **Claim (Weima):** 2:1–12 highlights missionaries’ holy/righteous/blameless conduct (2:10); 2:13–16 shifts to positive Thessalonian response (accepted word as word of God; suffered imitating Judean churches)—further confirming genuine character of apostle and mission-founding work.
- **Quote:** "That this response of the Thessalonian Christians was positive—they not only accepted the word of Paul as the word of God (2:13) but also were willing to be persecuted for this word, thereby imitating the persecuted churches in Judea (2:14–16)—further confirms the genuine character of the apostle and his mission-founding work in their midst."
- **Locus:** L21–23, L383–385 / 2:1–16
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-05 | Genre: autobiography at start of letter body after thanksgiving
- **Claim (Weima):** 2:1–16 (esp. 2:1–12) is autobiographical report: self-description of past activities; typically after thanksgiving (parallels Rom 1:11–16a; Gal 1:11–2:21; Phil 1:12–26 etc.). Traditional function: defend apostle and reaffirm authority so letter contents will be accepted.
- **Quote:** "The function of these autobiographical reports has been traditionally understood to be that of not merely informing readers about Paul’s life but also defending the apostle and reaffirming his authority over the letter recipients."
- **Locus:** L29–31 / 2:1–16 literary analysis
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-06 | Modern consensus (Malherbe/Lyons): exclusively paraenetic; Weima rejects
- **Claim (Weima reports + rejects):** Malherbe 1970 (Dio Chrysostom parallels; Cynic background) and Lyons 1985 shifted scholarship: antitheses as traditional topos, not actual accusations; function exemplary/paraenetic. Wide modern consensus abandons apologetic reading. Weima argues primary function remains defensive/apologetic (citing Weima 1997a; 2000b; Still; Holtz; Kim; Fee).
- **Quote:** "The widespread agreement among interpreters today is that the autobiographical statements of this passage have an exclusively exemplary or paraenetic function and that the traditional apologetic function is no longer a realistic option"
- **Locus:** L41–47 / Function of the Passage
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]]

### C-R2-07 | Five cumulative arguments for defensive function
- **Claim (Weima):** (1) Thanksgiving 1:5 unparalleled focus on Paul’s righteous character foreshadows 2:1–16; (2) apostolic parousia 2:17–3:10 parallels as *apologia pro absentia* to *apologia pro vita* of 2:1–16; (3) double God-as-witness (2:5, 10) and twofold passive *dokimazō* with God examining (2:4)—legal-like language; (4) frequency/emphasis of autobiographical antitheses (five in 2:1–8; threefold/fivefold negatives); (5) six appeals to firsthand knowledge of moral conduct (2:1, 2, 5, 9, 10, 11), not only prior teaching.
- **Quote:** "the cumulative effect of legitimizing the claim that the primary function of this passage is defensive or apologetic."
- **Locus:** L47–59 / Function of the Passage
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-08 | Extent: 2:1–16 coheres; 2:13–16 with past visit (not separate); authenticity assumed
- **Claim (Weima):** Beginning at 2:1 clear (disclosure formula, vocative, shift from thanksgiving). Ending: 2:13–16 belongs with 2:1–12 as past *eisodos*—Paul’s conduct then Thessalonians’ response—pattern already twice in 1:5–8 and 1:9–10. Supports: no eschatological climax at 2:12 (climax at 2:16); no transitional formula at 2:13; *kai* coordinating; *dia touto* anaphoric. **Authenticity of 2:13–16 assumed; full interpolation debate deferred to commentary introduction.**
- **Quote:** "this assumes the authenticity of 2:13–16 in contrast to the view that these verses are a non-Pauline interpolation; on this matter, see the commentary introduction."
- **Locus:** L61–67 / Extent of the Passage
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]]

### C-R2-09 | Structure of 2:1–16 (Weima outline)
- **Claim (Weima):** (1) Paul’s integrity 2:1–12: (a) bold preaching 2:1–2; (b) God-examined speech 2:3–4; (c) “innocent as an infant” 2:5–7b; (d) “loving as a nursing mother” 2:7c–8; (e) self-sufficient labor 2:9; (f) “nurturing as a father” 2:10–12. (2) Thessalonians’ response 2:13–16: (a) accepted word of Paul as word of God 2:13; (b) imitation of persecuted Judean churches 2:14–16. Prefers not subdividing 1–8 vs 9–12.
- **Quote:** "Paul’s defense of his past visit to Thessalonica in 2:1–16, therefore, possesses the following structure:"
- **Locus:** L69–99 / Structure of the Passage
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]]

### C-R2-10 | Opponents not inside church; charges on integrity via careful mirror reading
- **Claim (Weima):** Opponents outside (Timothy’s good report 3:6; exemplary lives; “hope and joy and crown”; “increase even more”; “brothers”; affectionate tone). Best candidates: *symphyletai* (2:14). Persecution = social harassment (refusal of civic/cultic participation), not primarily martyrdom. Mirror reading of antitheses (esp. 2:1–7b) with criteria yields defense against attacks on integrity/genuineness of motives—not method discarded (contra Lyons).
- **Quote:** "When these criteria are followed in a mirror reading of 2:1–12 and especially of the first four antithetical statements in 2:1–7b, the evidence leads clearly to the same conclusion: Paul is defending himself against attacks on his integrity and the genuineness of his motives."
- **Locus:** L111–117 / 2:1–12 intro
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[timothy]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### Group B — 2:1–4: bold preaching; God-examined speech; not flattery-type deception

### C-R2-11 | 2:1 kenē = “insincere,” not empty-handed or without results
- **Claim (Weima):** Three senses of *kenē*: (1) empty-handed (rejected—Paul’s figurative use elsewhere); (2) “in vain”/without results (fits 3:5 but not 2:2 focus); (3) “insincere” (preferred)—character of visit proved by bold preaching amid suffering. Theme for larger 2:1–16.
- **Quote:** "A few commentators view kenē as stressing the character of Paul’s past ministry in Thessalonica and so translate the term as “empty of purpose, lacking earnestness, insincere”"
- **Locus:** L121–133 / 2:1
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-12 | 2:2 Philippi suffering + great opposition prove sincerity
- **Claim (Weima):** Bold proclamation despite prior suffering and shameful mistreatment in Philippi (*hybristhentes* only here in Paul) and *en pollō agōni* in Thessalonica (external conflict, not mere exertion/anxiety). What charlatan would continue? Boldness *en tō theō hēmōn* = God as instrumental source; “gospel of God” subjective genitive.
- **Quote:** "After all, what charlatan would continue to subject himself to such abuse!"
- **Locus:** L135–143 / 2:2
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[silas]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-13 | 2:3–4: appeal not from deception, impure motive, or deceit; God-examined speech
- **Claim (Weima):** *Paraklēsis* = urgent missionary “appeal,” not consolation. Threefold denial: *planē* moral deception (not mere intellectual error); *akatharsia* general impure motive (not sexual misconduct charge—no evidence; Greco-Roman sexual tolerance); *dolos* baiting deceit (vs sophists). Positive: perfect passive *dedokimasmetha* by God to be entrusted with gospel; speak not people-pleasers but God-pleasers, God examining hearts (OT tester-of-hearts).
- **Quote:** "Paul’s strategy in the second antithetical statement of 2:3–4, therefore, is to defend the integrity of his preaching by appealing to his “God-examined speech.”"
- **Locus:** L147–195 / 2:3–4
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### Group C — Charges of flattery, greed, honor-seeking; infant metaphor (2:5–7b)

### C-R2-14 | 2:5–7b: three denials + parentheticals + affirmation “infants”
- **Claim (Weima):** Symmetric structure: Denial 1 flattery + “as you know”; Denial 2 greed + “God is our witness!”; Denial 3 demanding honor + 7a “even though we could have insisted…as apostles of Christ”; Affirmation 7b “but we became infants among you.” Modern translations wrongly end antithesis too early after “apostles of Christ” and adopt *ēpioi*.
- **Quote:** "most translations also wrongly adopt the reading “gentle” (ἤπιοι, ēpioi) in 2:7b instead of the more strongly attested reading “infants” (νήπιοι, nēpioi)."
- **Locus:** L197–237 / 2:5–7b
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]]

### C-R2-15 | Flattery (*kolakeia*): deceptive praise of traveling speakers
- **Claim (Weima):** Only NT use of *kolakeia*; Theophrastus/Aristotle/Philo/Plutarch/Dio: shameful profitable flattery. Paul denies mission-founding *logos* used empty praise/false promises; distances from street philosophers/rhetoricians. First aside: “as you know” (outward behavior observable).
- **Quote:** "The apostle denies that his original preaching to them … involved deceptive language, empty praise, or false promises to trick the hearers into accepting the gospel."
- **Locus:** L239–243 / 2:5
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-16 | Greed (*pleonexia*): financial; God as witness of inward motive
- **Claim (Weima):** *Prophasis* pejorative “pretext”; *pleonexia* here almost certainly financial (wandering preachers; later 2 Cor 9; Acts 20:33–35). Second aside: “God is [our] witness!”—rare in Paul; unparalleled second appeal at 2:10 with double *dokimazō* supports real defense.
- **Quote:** "The context of 1 Thess. 2:5, however, makes it almost certain that Paul is thinking specifically of financial greed, since wandering preachers of that day were typically accused of being interested solely in monetary gain."
- **Locus:** L245–249 / 2:5
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-17 | Honor (*doxa*): not demanding fame; *baros* = weight of authority not financial burden
- **Claim (Weima):** *Doxa* = fame/prestige (secular), not religious glory (contrast 2:12). *Zētountes* better “demanding” than mere seeking. Parenthetical *baros*: majority rightly “weight of authority/dignity” matching honor denial—not financial support (that arrives as new subject at 2:9).
- **Quote:** "The proper ground of this denial is not that Paul did not demand financial support but that he did not selfishly insist that honor (doxa) be given to him by the congregation."
- **Locus:** L251–259 / 2:6–7a
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-18 | Plural “apostles of Christ” includes Silvanus and Timothy
- **Claim (Weima):** First “apostle” in letter is plural—implies Silvanus and Timothy share apostolic status. Strongest solution: evolutionary use—no challenge to Paul’s apostleship yet, so free to include co-founders; later explicit about exclusive status under criticism. Rejects literary plural only-Paul; Silvanus-not-Timothy; and mere “messenger” sense (authority of Christ present).
- **Quote:** "as Paul feels free in the letter opening to bracket Silvanus and Timothy with himself on equal terms as cosenders (1:1), here too he has no hesitation to include them with him as “apostles of Christ.”"
- **Locus:** L261–269 / 2:7a
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[silas]], [[timothy]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-19 | Infant metaphor: innocence vs flattery/greed/honor
- **Claim (Weima):** First of three familial images (infants / nursing mother / father). *Nēpioi* contrasts whole 2:5–7a impure motives of wandering teachers; babies incapable of deceptive speech, ulterior motives, honor-seeking—innocence (Philo Spec. Laws 3.119). Fluid Pauline use (not always pejorative; 1 Cor 14:20 positive).
- **Quote:** "Babies are not capable of using deceptive speech, having ulterior motives, and being concerned with receiving honor; in all these things they are innocent."
- **Locus:** L271–277 / 2:7b
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### Group D — Nursing mother; workshop labor; father (2:7c–12)

### C-R2-20 | Nursing mother (*trophos*): love, not merely hired wet nurse
- **Claim (Weima):** *Trophos* properly nurse/wet nurse, but “her own children” reflexive + family metaphors push “nursing mother.” Love is key: rare *thalpō* “cherishes”; *homeiromenoi* deep yearning (attested only four times in Greek); share gospel of God and “our own selves” (*psychē* = very self, not physical life-laying-down); “you became beloved.” Deepest affective language in Pauline corpus (Wanamaker).
- **Quote:** "Whereas the first metaphor of infants highlights the innocence of Paul’s conduct and motives during his past visit to Thessalonica, the second metaphor of a nursing mother focuses on the love that Paul had for Thessalonian believers during his past visit."
- **Locus:** L281–313 / 2:7c–8
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-21 | 2:9 Self-sufficient labor night and day not to burden
- **Claim (Weima):** Fourth of six appeals to firsthand knowledge. *Kopos* + *mochthos* fixed pair = emphatic hard work. Night and day genitive = time within which (not hyperbolic whole day/night; order conventional). Purpose: *mē epibarēsai*—no material/financial burden. Explains loving self-gift (2:7c–8) more than merely revisiting greed denial. Accepts support later from established churches (Phil 4:15–16 while in Thessalonica).
- **Quote:** "During his mission-founding visit to Thessalonica, therefore, he worked hard (“Remember our labor and toil”) and long (“working night and day”) so that the new Christians in that city did not need to support him financially."
- **Locus:** L315–327 / 2:9
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-22 | Profession: leatherworker/tentmaker; workshop as evangelistic setting
- **Claim (Weima):** Clues: work “with our own hands” (1 Cor 4:12; Acts 20:34); Acts 18:3 *skēnopoioi*—better “leatherworker.” Rabbinic self-support tradition vs Hock/Malherbe Hellenistic philosopher parallel debated. Workshop as conventional setting for discourse: simultaneous work and preaching plausible, but present participle *ergazomenoi* marks aspect/continuity, not automatically simultaneity (Porter/Fanning).
- **Quote:** "During the long hours at his workbench, while cutting and sewing leather to make tents and other related goods, Paul was not only supporting himself but also sharing the gospel with fellow workers and customers"
- **Locus:** L323–329 / 2:9
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-23 | 2:10–12 Father metaphor: holy/righteous/blameless; nurturing instruction
- **Claim (Weima):** Fifth appeal + second God-as-witness; three nearly synonymous adverbs emphasize irreproachable conduct (not sharp God-vs-humans classical split). Father metaphor = nurturing/instructional role (vs mother = affection); three participles appealing/encouraging/imploring piled for emphasis. Purpose: walk worthily of God who is calling (present) into own kingdom and glory—response not earning salvation; kingdom language agrees with Acts 17:6–7 charges.
- **Quote:** "Whereas the first metaphor of infants (2:7b) highlights the innocence of Paul during his mission-founding visit and the second metaphor of a nursing mother (2:7c) stresses the love that motivated the apostle during that same visit, this third metaphor of a father conveys the nurturing role that Paul had during his stay."
- **Locus:** L331–381 / 2:10–12
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### Group E — 2:13 Word of God; 2:14–16 Judeans, wrath, ephthasen

### C-R2-24 | 2:13: received/accepted Paul’s word as truly word of God, still at work
- **Claim (Weima):** *Kai* + *dia touto* link 2:13–16 to 2:1–12 (*dia touto* anaphoric to gospel mediation generally; second *kai* = “indeed” emphasizing thanksgiving). *Hoti* epexegetical not additional causal ground. *Paralambanō* + *dechomai*: technical reception of tradition vs internal appropriation (“took” and “took to it”—Gaventa). Explicit: not word of humans but word of God; relative *hos* = word (not God) still *energeitai* in believers (faith required).
- **Quote:** "There is no difference between Paul’s word and God’s word. The gospel that the apostle proclaimed during his original ministry in Thessalonica … was no mere human word but instead was the divine word of God."
- **Locus:** L389–417 / 2:13
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-25 | 2:14 Imitation of Judean churches via same-type suffering from fellow citizens
- **Claim (Weima):** Second positive response: willingness to suffer for the word; *gar* proves 2:13. Imitation foreshadowed 1:6 but object now Judean churches “of God … in Judea … in Christ Jesus.” Judea = broader Palestine. Comparative: same things from own *symphyletai* as they from *Ioudaioi*.
- **Quote:** "the specific way in which the Thessalonians have imitated the Judean churches is through the suffering they have endured for their newfound faith."
- **Locus:** L419–443 / 2:14
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-26 | Why Judea; Zealot-era persecution of Judean churches (late 40s–early 50s)
- **Claim (Weima):** Why remote Judean churches? Most likely: place Thessalonians in long line of Palestinian persecuted (prophets, Jesus, earliest Christians, Paul). Best historical setting for Judean suffering: late 40s–early 50s Zealot purging of Gentile influence under Tiberius Julius Alexander and Ventidius Cumanus (not early-30s Paul-as-persecutor only; not only Herod Agrippa leaders). May illuminate harsh 2:15–16.
- **Quote:** "the best option is that Paul has in view the late 40s and very early 50s—a period that not only came immediately before the writing of 1 Thessalonians … but also witnessed a rising Zealot movement in Palestine"
- **Locus:** L445–447 / 2:14
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-27 | *Symphyletai* geographical (Thessalonian inhabitants incl. some Jews); *Ioudaioi* = Judeans (restrictive)
- **Claim (Weima):** *Symphyletai* hapax: not purely ethnic Gentile-only; geographical inhabitants of Thessalonica (mostly Gentiles, some Jews)—fits Acts 17:5–9 Jewish-instigated civic unrest. *Ioudaioi*: local/geographical “Judeans” via prior “in Judea”; not all Jews—only those participating in 2:15–16 activities; remove comma after “Jews” (restrictive, not general). Not anti-Semitic against Jewish people *in toto* (Judean churches and Paul are Jews).
- **Quote:** "Paul, therefore, does not have all Jews in view but only those in Judea—the “Judeans” (Bruce 1982: 46: “One could translate Ἰουδαῖοι here as ‘Judeans’”)."
- **Locus:** L449–453 / 2:14
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-28 | 2:15–16 dual function: prepare absence defense + encourage under persecution
- **Claim (Weima):** By end of v. 14 apology of 2:1–12 reaches a close; “the Jews” occasions presynoptic traditional material serving (1) explain inability to return—Jews “drove us out” → 2:17–20; (2) encourage steadfastness under opposition → 3:1–5 (shared with prophets, Jesus, Judean churches, Paul).
- **Quote:** "This traditional material functions first to explain why Paul has not been able to return for a second “visit” (εἴσοδος, eisodos) to Thessalonica: the Jews “who drove us out” (v. 15)"
- **Locus:** L455–457 / 2:15–16 intro
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-29 | Four clauses on certain Judeans: killed Lord Jesus and prophets; drove us out; do not please God; hostile to all
- **Claim (Weima):** Fixed pattern: *kai* + emphatic object + attributive participle. “Killed” (not crucified) from prophets-killing tradition; unusual order Lord Jesus then prophets emphasizes heinousness of killing “the Lord.” Prophets = OT prophets (reject NT-martyr and “drove out prophets and us” re-parsing). *Ekdiōxantōn* aorist: drive out—best Thessalonica-specific (Acts 17:5–10; 2:17). “Not please God” serious Pauline ethical charge (present tense continuous). Hostility theological (hindering Gentile mission), not pagan social antisemitism catalogs.
- **Quote:** "Yet there is an important difference between all these harsh statements about the Jews and that of the apostle: “Pagan criticism was social, Paul’s is theological” (Malherbe 2000: 170)."
- **Locus:** L459–483 / 2:15–16a
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-30 | 2:16: hindering Gentile salvation; constantly filling measure of sins
- **Claim (Weima):** Participle subordinate to “hostile”: by hindering speaking to Gentiles that they may be saved. Present *kōlyontōn* = persistent multi-locale opposition (vs Thessalonica-specific “drove out”). *Eis to anaplērōsai* + *pantote*: result (prefer) of whole 15–16a series; aorist views continuous filling collectively; cup/vessel of sins then judgment (Gen 15:16; Matt 23:32; Jewish conventional language against faithless co-nationals).
- **Quote:** "throughout history there have been some Jews—whether the Judeans of Paul’s day who persecuted the churches or earlier Jews who opposed the OT prophets and were involved in the killing of the Lord Jesus—whose disobedience against God and his spokespersons have resulted in the constant filling up of their nation’s sins."
- **Locus:** L485–495 / 2:16
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-31 | *Ephthasen* wrath has come (past); *eis telos* “until the end”
- **Claim (Weima):** *Phthanō* here “arrive/reach,” not prophetic aorist future; not weakened “has drawn near.” Both present and future wrath in Paul’s framework (Rom 1:18; 1:10; 5:9). Historical referent of past wrath unknowable with probability (options: Cross climax; Claudius AD 49 expulsion; Jerusalem massacre AD 49; famine; Theudas; Agrippa’s death; AD 70 fall—esp. prophetic-aorist or **interpolation advocates Baur/Pearson**; general rejection of gospel). Many prefer Claudius expulsion (near letter date; Aquila/Priscilla to Corinth). *Eis telos* temporal, parallel *pantote*; prefer “until the end” (until Christ’s return) over “at last/forever/fully,” given Rom 11:25–32 future for Israel—does not spell out post-end fate of rebellious Israel.
- **Quote:** "Paul therefore claims that the wrath of God has come upon his people “until the end,” meaning until the day of Christ’s return"
- **Locus:** L497–513 / 2:16c
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-32 | Interpolation debate in-range footprint only (deferral + AD 70/Pearson)
- **Claim (Weima, limited to this range):** Unit delimitation assumes 2:13–16 authentic; full case vs non-Pauline interpolation is in commentary introduction (not this slice). Separately, fall of Jerusalem AD 70 is proposed by those who take *ephthasen* as prophetic aorist **and** by those who hold 2:13[14]–16 a later interpolation (Baur 1875; Pearson 1971). **Not in range:** Weima’s four arguments (theological, historical, form-critical, linguistic) against interpolation.
- **Quote:** "The fall of Jerusalem and the destruction of the temple in AD 70 is frequently proposed by both those who view the verb ephthasen as a prophetic aorist … and those who believe 2:13[14]–16 to be a later interpolation (so, e.g., Baur 1875: 87–88; Pearson 1971: 82–84)."
- **Locus:** L65; L507 / 2:13–16 extent; 2:16 wrath options
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]]

### Group F — Excursus 2: 2:7 nēpioi vs ēpioi

### C-R2-33 | External evidence decisively favors νήπιοι (infants)
- **Claim (Weima):** Oldest Greek witnesses all have *nēpioi* (𝔓65 3rd c.; א* B 4th; C* D* I 5th); Old Latin, Sahidic MS, Bohairic, Clement/Origen/Ambst. Oldest *ēpioi* = A 5th c. (~200 years later). Majority Alexandrian + Western; early West and East. NA/UBS shifted toward infants. Even *ēpioi* advocates admit external evidence decisive for *nēpioi* (Fee: under ordinary circumstances no one would accept *ēpioi*).
- **Quote:** "What is immediately striking about the external evidence is how strongly it supports the reading “infants.”"
- **Locus:** L543–557 / Excursus 2 External Evidence
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]]

### C-R2-34 | Four internal arguments for ἤπιοι fail
- **Claim (Weima):** (1) Dittography for *nēpioi* dismissible—haplography equally possible; cannot decide originality. (2) *Ēpioi* not rare enough that scribes would replace with common *nēpioi*—neither very common in Paul/NT; *ēpios* well-known virtue outside Bible (Malherbe; computer searches). (3) Paul not always pejorative with *nēpios* (1 Cor 3:1 neg; 13:11 neutral; 14:20 positive *nēpiazō*); LXX/Gospels/Philo positive innocence. (4) Mixed metaphor “infants→nurse” mitigated by punctuation, lectio difficilior, Pauline rapid metaphor shifts (Gal 4:19; 2 Cor 2:14; within 1 Thess 2 mother/father/orphan).
- **Quote:** "An evaluation of each of these four arguments reveals that they do not provide, neither individually nor even collectively, the needed justification for rejecting the clear testimony of the external evidence."
- **Locus:** L559–637 / Excursus 2 Internal Evidence
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]]

### C-R2-35 | Correct punctuation: full stop after “infants among you”
- **Claim (Weima):** UBS/NA and major ET wrongly place full stop after “apostles of Christ,” starting new sentence at 7b—producing mixed metaphor in one sentence. Grammar demands period after 7b “but we became infants among you”: (a) *alla* after negative completes *ou…alla* antithesis (five such in 2:1–8); (b) *hōs…houtōs* correlative in 7c–8 (not *houtōs* as degree adverb “so deeply”—no exact Pauline parallel). Infants conclude 2:5–7b; nursing mother opens 2:7c–8—separate sentences, distinct functions.
- **Quote:** "a full stop (period) be placed after the phrase “but we became infants among you” in 2:7b so that the infant metaphor concludes the clause of 2:5–7b. Then the nursing-mother metaphor introduces the clause of 2:7c–8."
- **Locus:** L583–627 / Excursus 2 Argument 4 / punctuation
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]]

### C-R2-36 | Orphan metaphor 2:17 supports infant reading
- **Claim (Weima):** *Aporphanizō* in extant Greek always children orphaned from parents, never parents from children (Faulkenberry Miller 1999)—so 2:17 = Paul/co-workers as orphaned children. Supports *nēpioi*: inverted metaphors (father→orphan; infant→mother) feasible; non-authoritative self-portrayal confident; orphan more natural extension of prior child image.
- **Quote:** "By using the verbal form ἀπορφανισθέντες, Paul presents himself and his coworkers as children whose forced departure from Thessalonica has meant that they are orphaned from the believers in that city."
- **Locus:** L631–637 / Excursus 2
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[paul-apostle]], [[jeffrey-weima]]

### C-R2-37 | Excursus conclusion: allow “we became infants among you”
- **Claim (Weima):** Debate less ambiguous than usually portrayed; external decisive; internal fails to override; superior reading *nēpioi* is striking innocence metaphor effective in 2:5–7b argument.
- **Quote:** "There are compelling reasons, therefore, for allowing Paul to make the claim of innocence that he made to the Thessalonians long ago: “But we became infants among you.”"
- **Locus:** L641–643 / Excursus 2 Conclusion
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]]

### Group G — Additional notes / textual minutiae (select)

### C-R2-38 | Select Additional Notes (2:8–16 apparatus)
- **Claim (Weima):** 2:8 *homeiromenoi* vs classical *himeiromenoi* same meaning; *eudokoumen* best imperfect (past visit; some MSS aorist); gospel “of Christ” minority vs “of God.” 2:9 explanatory *gar* added in some MSS. 2:12 present *kalountos* strongly supported (aorist under Gal 1:6 influence—Metzger). 2:13 first *kai* omitted late MSS; strongly supported. 2:15 *idious* prophets secondary (strengthen OT-prophet reading). 2:16 *tou theou* with wrath late/few—not original but ET “of God” warranted; perfect *ephthaken* minority vs aorist *ephthasen*.
- **Quote:** "The present tense καλοῦντος, which is appropriate in the context, is strongly supported by B D F G H K L P and most minuscules."
- **Locus:** L517–537 / Additional Notes
- **Targets:** [[1-thessalonians]], [[jeffrey-weima]], [[weima-1-2-thessalonians-becnt]]
